So we're pulling the trigger a couple of weeks early, just so we could spend a few minutes talking about the latest serious threat, very serious threat to your healthcare. And it's called Cassidy Graham. So what is Cassidy Graham? Well, it is a bill put forth by Republican senators Lindsey Graham and Bill Cassidy. And it is designed to fulfill the seven year promise of repealing and replacing the Affordable Care Act, which most people know as Obamacare. And why is Cassidy Graham happening right now? Well, without getting too deep into the legislative maneuvers, The Republican leadership in Congress has until September 30th. That is their deadline to be able to pass a bill like this with a simple majority vote. So things have to happen by September 30th or the goal of repealing Obamacare becomes much more difficult to attain. And what does Cassidy Graham do? Why is that bill such a serious threat? Well, as I said, it repeals most of the Affordable Care Act. And specifically, it repeals most of the protections and mandates that are part of the act and basically leaves everything up to each individual state to decide what they want to do. So each state can decide whether people with preexisting conditions are going to be covered at all. or whether they might be put into a hugely expensive high risk pool, which was the exact kind of thing that was done before the Affordable Care Act became law. And those high risk pools, by the way, they failed over and over and over again. Cassidy Graham leaves it up to each state to decide whether there are going to be annual or lifetime caps on the amount of benefits each of us is entitled to, which if you're battling a chronic illness, if you are requiring long-term treatment, the idea of annual caps and lifetime caps is something you literally can't live with. What's the problem with Cassidy Graham? The problem is in the details. because there aren't any. We just don't know what each state will do. But we do know that the bill doesn't require them to do anything. We don't know how many people are going to lose their health insurance under this bill. And the reason we don't know that is because unlike every other piece of legislation that Congress deals with, The Republican congressional leadership can't wait for the nonpartisan congressional budget office to audit and score this bill and tell us things like what it will cost, who will be affected, and how it's going to impact all of us. And the reason they won't be scoring the bill is because they can't get it done by the September 30th deadline. And getting the vote done by that deadline seems to be the most important thing here. But the Brookings Institute released an independent analysis last week that indicated that 21 million Americans are going to lose their health insurance over the next 10 years if Cassidy Graham becomes law. So that's something we do know. And so for some combination of all of these reasons and more reasons that we won't even get into right now, the American Medical Association has come out against this bill. as has Kaiser Permanente, as has the American Hospital Association, as has the American Heart Association, the March of Dimes, the ALS Association, the Alzheimer's Association, the American Cancer Society, the American College of Physicians, the American Diabetes Association, the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Lung Association, the American Psychiatric Association, the Arthritis Foundation, the Autism Foundation, Blue Cross Blue Shield, one of the largest insurers in the country, has come out against the bill, the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation, the Infectious Diseases Society of America, the National Association of Medicaid Directors, the National Institute for Reproductive Health, Planned Parenthood, the National Kidney Foundation, and the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. All of these groups have found Cassidy Graham to be bad medicine. So, in all of this doom and gloom, is there any good news? There is a bit. And that is amazing news.
